city.name: Antwerp
city.ticket_note: one De Lijn ticket also covers the trams

scoring: score = sum of POI weights (must-see sights count 2.5x) + 1.5 x distinct 700 m district cells those POIs fall in, so both geographic spread and headline sights can outrank raw count

all_pois.name: AMUZ (St. Augustine's Church)
all_pois.description: Deconsecrated baroque church turned concert hall for early music.

all_pois.name: Antwerp Central Station
all_pois.description: The 'railway cathedral' — a stone-and-iron dome over four levels of platforms.

all_pois.name: Antwerp Zoo
all_pois.description: Founded 1843, right beside Central Station — one of the oldest zoos in the world.

all_pois.name: Boerentoren
all_pois.description: Europe's first skyscraper (1932), an art-deco slab over the Meir.

all_pois.name: Bourla Theatre
all_pois.description: 1834 neoclassical playhouse, the last surviving continental theatre of its type.

all_pois.name: Brewers' House
all_pois.description: 16th-century water house that pumped the city's brewing water, with machinery intact.

all_pois.name: Cathedral of Our Lady
all_pois.description: Belgium's tallest cathedral — 123m of Brabantine Gothic, with four Rubens altarpieces inside.

all_pois.name: City Hall
all_pois.description: 1560s Renaissance city hall on the Grote Markt, a UNESCO-listed civic landmark.

all_pois.name: DIVA
all_pois.description: Museum of diamonds, silver and jewellery, in a townhouse off the Grote Markt.

all_pois.name: De Koninck City Brewery
all_pois.description: The bolleke brewery, with a tasting room and food hall in the old stables.

all_pois.name: Diamond District
all_pois.description: Four streets behind the station through which most of the world's rough diamonds pass.

all_pois.name: FOMU (Photo Museum)
all_pois.description: One of Europe's serious photography museums, with a 3-million-image collection.

all_pois.name: Grote Markt
all_pois.description: The guildhall-lined main square, with the Brabo fountain flinging a severed hand at its centre.

all_pois.name: Handelsbeurs
all_pois.description: The world's first purpose-built commodity exchange, reopened after a long restoration.

all_pois.name: Hendrik Conscienceplein
all_pois.description: Antwerp's most complete baroque square, car-free and lit by gas lamps.

all_pois.name: Het Steen
all_pois.description: The 13th-century riverside castle — Antwerp's oldest building, now the visitor centre.

all_pois.name: Koning Albertpark
all_pois.description: Green wedge along the southern ring, good for a breather between museums.

all_pois.name: Koningin Astridplein
all_pois.description: The square in front of Central Station, gateway to the zoo and the diamond quarter.

all_pois.name: Law Courts
all_pois.description: Richard Rogers' 'sails' over the southern approach — a modern city gate.

all_pois.name: Loodswezen
all_pois.description: Neo-Gothic pilotage building on the quay, a Scheldt-front landmark.

all_pois.name: M HKA
all_pois.osm_name: M HKA - Museum van Hedendaagse Kunst Antwerpen
all_pois.description: Antwerp's contemporary art museum, in a converted grain silo on the Zuid waterfront.

all_pois.name: MAS | Museum aan de Stroom
all_pois.description: Ten stacked red-sandstone boxes; the free rooftop spiral is the best view in Antwerp.

all_pois.name: Maagdenhuis
all_pois.description: Former foundling girls' orphanage, now a small museum of Flemish masters and food bowls.

all_pois.name: MoMu (Fashion Museum)
all_pois.description: Belgium's fashion museum — home turf of the Antwerp Six, reopened in 2021.

all_pois.name: Park Spoor Noord
all_pois.description: A 24-hectare park laid over a demolished railway yard — the city's favourite new green space.

all_pois.name: Plantin-Moretus Museum
all_pois.description: UNESCO-listed printing house with the two oldest surviving printing presses in the world.

all_pois.name: Port House
all_pois.description: Zaha Hadid's glass diamond balanced on a replica Hanseatic fire station.

all_pois.name: Red Star Line Museum
all_pois.description: In the sheds where two million emigrants were deloused before sailing to New York.

all_pois.name: Royal Museum of Fine Arts (KMSKA)
all_pois.osm_name: Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten Antwerpen
all_pois.description: Reopened in 2022 after eleven years — Van Eyck, Memling, Ensor and Rubens at full scale.

all_pois.name: Royal Palace (Paleis op de Meir)
all_pois.description: Napoleon's Antwerp residence on the shopping street, with a chocolate salon downstairs.

all_pois.name: Rubens House
all_pois.description: The painter's own home and studio, with an Italianate portico he designed himself.

all_pois.name: Ruihuis
all_pois.description: Entrance to the Ruien — the covered medieval canals running under the old town.

all_pois.name: Sint-Felixpakhuis
all_pois.description: Vast 1860s warehouse split by a covered street; now the city archive.

all_pois.name: Snijders&Rockox House
all_pois.description: The patrician home of Rubens' patron, hung as a 17th-century collector would have had it.

all_pois.name: St. Andrew's Church
all_pois.description: Parish church of the old Sint-Andries quarter, with a memorial to Mary, Queen of Scots.

all_pois.name: St. Anna Pedestrian Tunnel
all_pois.description: 1933 tunnel under the Scheldt, reached by the original wooden escalators.

all_pois.name: St. Charles Borromeo Church
all_pois.description: Baroque church whose façade Rubens helped design; the ceiling paintings burned in 1718.

all_pois.name: St. George's Church
all_pois.description: Neo-Gothic parish church on the line of the old city walls.

all_pois.name: St. James' Church
all_pois.description: Rubens' burial place, and the richest church interior in the city.

all_pois.name: St. Paul's Church
all_pois.description: Gothic Dominican church with a startling baroque calvary garden tucked beside it.

all_pois.name: Stadspark
all_pois.description: Romantic 19th-century park on the line of the old Spanish ramparts.

all_pois.name: Vleeshuis
all_pois.description: The butchers' guildhall of 1504, striped like streaky bacon; now a music museum.

all_pois.name: Zuiderpershuis
all_pois.description: Neo-Gothic hydraulic power station of 1882, now a world-music venue.
